title: Obesity, morbid obesity and BMI
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's weight diagnosis and BMI, if reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Weight management and obesity.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting today for a follow-up visit to discuss his weight. He reports that he has struggled to lose weight despite some intermittent efforts at lifestyle modifications. He expresses a desire to lose weight to improve his overall health and mobility. He currently engages in minimal physical activity and reports a diet high in processed carbohydrates. He denies any acute symptoms or specific physical limitations today.

Medication List
Multivitamin, daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. He appears in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable. BMI 37.8. Heart rate is 72 bpm. Blood pressure is 130/82 mmHg. Respiratory rate is 16. Temperature is 98.6 F. Physical exam reveals no new areas of concern.

Assessment
The patient has obesity. He is motivated to make changes but requires structured guidance.

Plan
We discussed a comprehensive weight management plan. I provided counseling on caloric restriction and emphasized the importance of increasing daily physical activity, specifically aiming for 30 minutes of walking most days. We will meet again in three months to monitor progress.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C
October 14, 2026
explanations: Obesity documented by the provider: E66.9. The coder does not upgrade it to morbid obesity from the BMI.
BMI 37.x with a provider weight diagnosis: add Z68.37.

distractors.why: Only the provider can diagnose morbid obesity; the BMI does not change the diagnosis.
The BMI is documented and the provider diagnosed the weight condition: add the Z68 code.
